vendored: site/favicons/* and site/images/silverballmania-mark.svg (copied from canon assets/favicons and assets/logos; re-copy when the canon's mark changes)

divergences.what: Overlay defaults to the system's light block, not dark
divergences.why: Redlining floats over arbitrary host apps as a tool; light was chosen as the default on 2026-09-06. Dark stays available and is the system's identity, so nothing in the light block is restyled.

divergences.what: Brand assets: only the mark is adopted, for the docs site (header and favicon set); wordmark, lockup, broadcast and instructional layers are not
divergences.why: Redlining is its own npm package with its own name, but it is made under the silverballmania brand: since 2026-09-08 the mark sits beside the red wordmark in the site header and is the favicon set under site/favicons/. The user chose the canon's own black-and-white variant (silverballmania-mark-black.svg: black disc, white turbine) over the green primary, so the site reads as black, white and red; the PNG favicons and the single-PNG .ico were rendered from that SVG with Chromium. The mark is never recoloured beyond the canon's own variants and never mirrored. The overlay itself carries no logo.

divergences.what: Fonts resolve to system fallbacks unless the host app already loads Space Grotesk / Inter
divergences.why: PRD section 13: nothing leaves the machine. The canon's Google Fonts @import and the Montserrat @font-face are stripped from the vendored copy; the token fallback stacks apply.

divergences.what: No Tailwind in the overlay; component styles are hand-written CSS on the vendored tokens
divergences.why: The overlay is a small shadow-scoped UI; a Tailwind compile step would add build complexity for a dozen classes. The PRD listed Tailwind 4; the tokens, not the utility layer, carry the design.

divergences.what: Accent is a redline red (#9e2018 fill, #b92b22 / #66150f text) instead of the canon's green
divergences.why: Chosen by the user on 2026-09-08, darkened one step on request the same day: the product is called Redlining and its marks should read as red lines. Applied as an override of the --sbm-green ramp in src/overlay/styles.ts (brandCss) after the vendored tokens, so every semantic accent token follows and both themes keep the canon's lightness steps; the burned-in screenshot pins and site.css use the same values. Nothing else in the palette changes.

gaps.what: Port Button, IconButton, Tooltip, Toast, Dialog, ConfirmDialog, Badge, Textarea from canon components/{core,overlay}/*.jsx into src/overlay/ui/ as TSX. Tooltip, Dialog and Toast portal to document.body in the canon; in Redlining they must portal to the shadow root

Toolbar, numbered pins, hover badge, note popover and list panel have no canon component. Build on tokens: pins rounded-full on --color-accent-fill with --color-on-accent; hover outline 2px --color-border-focus; popover radius-xl, shadow-2, --color-background-overlay; list panel 320px on --color-background-elevated
Re-measure contrast for pin labels and hover badges. The canon's claims are measured on its own four surfaces; the overlay adds a fifth, the host page under a scrim

notes: Overlay built 2026-09-06 on the vendored tokens. Remaining gaps: G4 (port canon components — the overlay uses its own small set), G5 (spec review of pins/popover/panel against the canon), G7 (contrast re-measure over host pages). D5 (red accent) added 2026-09-08.

applied.what: tokens.css vendored as a CSS string, comments and broadcast section stripped; theme.css and base.css not vendored (no Tailwind in the overlay; overlay CSS is hand-written on the tokens)
:root → :host and [data-theme=light] → :host([data-theme=light]) applied by the vendor script; the shadow host carries data-theme="light" by default
Google Fonts @import and Montserrat @font-face stripped; fallback stacks apply
theme prop on <Redlining /> (light | dark), light default
